text:
[title] Block tables
[body] KV-cache split into fixed-size blocks, mapped per sequence
[body] Copy-on-write shares blocks across parallel samples
[body] Prefix caching hit rate: 61% on the chat workload

novice.takeaway: The slide describes a memory management technique called 'block tables' that splits and shares cached data to improve efficiency in serving AI models.
questions: How does prefix caching improve performance?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe this block table method contributes to the claimed 2.4x efficiency gain.

peer.takeaway: The system manages a per-sequence key-value cache using fixed-size blocks with copy-on-write sharing and prefix caching to improve memory efficiency.
questions: What counts as a 'block' size in practice?
How does prefix caching relate to the 61% hit rate?
How do block tables address the earlier fragmentation problem?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe block tables efficiently manage memory to boost throughput.

expert.takeaway: The slide describes PagedAttention-style block tables for KV-cache management, enabling copy-on-write sharing and reporting a 61% prefix cache hit rate on a chat workload.
questions: How is the 61% hit rate measured/defined?
How does block table overhead compare to contiguous KV-cache?
expert.inferred_claim: The presenter wants us to believe block tables with copy-on-write and prefix caching contribute to the claimed goodput gains.
